crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Protein Structure Prediction
children.blurb: Protein structure prediction is the computational task of determining the three-dimensional shape of a protein from its amino acid sequence.

children.name: Designing New Molecules
children.blurb: Designing new molecules is the use of computational methods to propose chemical structures that could become drugs, agrochemicals, or materials.

children.name: Simulated Clinical Trials
children.blurb: Simulated clinical trials use computational models to estimate how a treatment might behave in people before, alongside, or instead of some parts of a physical trial.

children.name: Toxicity Forecasting
children.blurb: Toxicity forecasting in drug discovery predicts whether a candidate molecule or biologic will cause harm in humans, covering endpoints such as liver injury, heart rhythm effects, kidney damage, skin sensitization, and genotoxicity.

children.name: Drug Repurposing
children.blurb: Drug repurposing is the search for new therapeutic uses for compounds that already have some safety or manufacturing history.

sections.body: Drug discovery and molecular simulation is the use of artificial intelligence to work out the shapes of proteins, propose new chemical compounds, estimate how those compounds behave in the body, and search existing drugs for uses they were not originally approved for. In practice the work is mostly prediction and ranking rather than discovery on its own. A model can suggest a molecule that binds a target, flag a compound likely to be toxic, or propose a protein fold, and each of those outputs then has to be tested in a laboratory. The field sits inside the wider set of scientific models this site tracks, which currently number 804 alongside 1000 medical AI models. The promise is speed and cost, and the reality is that most candidates still fail somewhere in the pipeline.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Protein structure prediction is the most settled part of the field, with models producing folds that often match experimental structures closely enough to be useful, though they still struggle with flexible regions, multiple states and complexes. Molecule design generates vast numbers of candidates, but generated molecules are only hypotheses until synthesised and assayed, and synthesis itself is a bottleneck. Simulated clinical trials can model patient populations and flag design problems before a real trial runs, yet they cannot substitute for a real trial and their outputs depend heavily on assumptions in the model. Toxicity forecasting catches some signals early but misses rare and idiosyncratic reactions, and drug repurposing has produced genuine successes alongside many failures. The honest limit across all of it is that prediction is not evidence, and the gap between a promising score and a working medicine remains wide.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the pipeline from target to candidate to test. Protein Structure Prediction comes first, because knowing the shape of a target is what makes the rest possible. Designing New Molecules takes that structural knowledge and generates compounds that might act on it. Toxicity Forecasting sits alongside design, screening those compounds for likely harm before anyone commits to making them. Simulated Clinical Trials then model how a candidate might behave across a patient population, which is where trial design questions get asked early. Drug Repurposing runs somewhat in parallel, taking compounds already known to be safe in humans and asking whether they act on a different target. Read together they describe a chain of predictions, each one narrowing the field before real experiments begin.
